subject: Perimeter isolation storyboard for Greenline — SOC 2 evidence request
messages:
From: Rachel Ortega <rachel.ortega@greenline.com>

Cc: Greenline Security <security@greenline.com>, Tom Adler <tom.adler@vendorprocure.io>

Subject: SOC 2: request for perimeter/isolation storyboard for Dedicated & Private

Jordan —

Thanks for the run-through last week. As part of our SOC 2 scoping the auditors asked for a short, annotated storyboard that explains how Redwood enforces perimeter isolation between the control plane and customer compute for both Dedicated (reserved pools) and Private (VPC-onboarding) deployments.

Key asks from our side:
- A simple sequence storyboard (client request -> routing -> model variant selection -> model execution -> responses) showing which segments are customer-managed vs Redwood-managed.
- Markers for where KV cache and prefix caching live, and whether any shared services touch customer data.
- A short callout on network egress controls and KMS boundary for Private deployments.
- Any mitigations you use to guarantee data-plane isolation during autoscaling or failover.

Can you provide a one-page storyboard + an annotated checklist we can drop into our audit packet? Ideally PDF and a copy with inline comments for our reviewers.

Thanks,
Rachel Ortega
Security Program Manager — Greenline Financial
[attachment: greenline-soc2-questions-annotated.xlsx (24KB)]

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Rachel Ortega <rachel.ortega@greenline.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2: request for perimeter/isolation storyboard for Dedicated & Private

Rachel —

Appreciate the clarity. Attaching a first-draft storyboard (PDF) and a short write-up that maps each storyboard frame to SOC 2 control areas (CC6, CC7, etc.). High-level notes up front:

- We explicitly separate the control plane (Redwood-managed) from customer compute in both deployment modes. For Dedicated we run tenant processes inside reserved GPU pools in a logically isolated tenant slice with enforced network ACLs and per-tenant identities. For Private (VPC) the data plane is hosted in the customer's VPC or private subnet with customer-managed routing; the control plane remains in a customer-specific, isolated project in Redwood’s control environment.
- Prefix/KV caches are scoped to model instance and tenant; no cross-tenant cache sharing.
- KMS usage: in Private deployments we integrate customer KMS for encryption-at-rest keys (optional). In Dedicated we use per-tenant keys managed by Redwood KMS unless customer opts for BYOK.
- Autoscaling/failover: we snapshot KV caches to ephemeral encrypted stores and enforce cryptographic shredding on deprovision; scaling events are orchestrated via isolated worker pools per-tenant to avoid noisy-neighbor leakage.

Attached: redwood-perimeter-storyboard-v1.pdf (contains sequence frames + callouts) and a one-page checklist.

If you want, Kimberly and Mina can add the network ACL snippets and an explicit example of the TCP/UDP port set we use for inter-service comms.

Next steps:
1) You review and mark up the PDF (comments preferred).
2) We add any network snippets you need and return an annotated version.
3) Finalize for your audit packet.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Director, Solutions Architecture — Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Forwarding quick network snippets for the storyboard frames. Put these into the PDF as an appendix (short, copyable ACL and routing examples):

--- network appendix (to paste into storyboard) ---
Frame A: Ingress (client -> Redwood edge LB)
- Public LB terminates TLS, forwards requests to per-region ingress fleet over mTLS.
- In Dedicated: ingress LB routes to tenant-specific pool via route-table lookup; no cross-tenant NAT.
- In Private (VPC): ingress is via account VPC peering/VPN; control-plane egress flows from control namespace to customer VPC through an explicit egress gateway with ACLs restricted to port 443 and internal management ports (SSH only for bastion, disabled by default).

Frame B: Routing & Model Selection
- Routing policy tag: {region, cost-tier, latency-slo} applied in control plane.
- Model variants run under per-tenant runtime identity; KV cache mount is bound to runtime identity.

Frame C: Execution & KV Cache
- KV/prefix caches are ephemeral, encrypted, and stored on tenant-scoped ephemeral volumes.
- No shared memory between tenant runtimes; inter-process communication uses authenticated RPC over mutual TLS inside the tenancy boundary.

Frame D: Autoscale / Failover
- New worker nodes bootstrap from encrypted image; keys provisioned via short-lived tokens.
- Cache shredding routine: on decommission, zeroize and rotate disk keys.

Ask: Jordan — do you want the ACL snippets formatted for Azure NSG and GCP VPC firewall rules? I can add them if Greenline needs vendor-specific text.

-Kim

Thanks, this looks good and exactly the level of detail our auditors wanted. A couple of small follow-ups from the security review team:

1) Can you confirm whether there are any async message queues (e.g., Kafka) that transiently store inference inputs in the control plane for Dedicated? If yes, we need retention and encryption details.
2) For the Private option: can you add an explicit KMS usage note that shows the different key hierarchies when customer brings their own keys vs Redwood-managed keys?
3) Please add a short line in Frame D that explains how HA failover avoids rehydrating another tenant's cache on the same disk (we need an explicit statement about ephemeral volume reuse prevention).

If you can add an updated PDF with those three callouts, we can slot it into our SOC 2 packet tomorrow.
